title: Enterprise Onboarding, Escalation, Integration, and QBR Playbook
author: Priya Sharma
summary: Operational playbook for enterprise onboarding, support escalation, integration guidance, known issues/workarounds, and QBR/health-check materials for Customer Success teams working with Redwood Inference enterprise customers.
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates the operational runbooks and templates the Customer Success (CS) team uses for enterprise onboarding, first-line support, escalation, technical integration handoffs, and quarterly business reviews (QBRs). It is intended for CS, Solutions Engineering, Support, and SRE partners.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-success for enterprise customers to under 14 days (target for standard integrations).
- Provide a clear, rapid escalation path to maintain 99.9% availability for customer-facing inference endpoints.
- Standardize QBR preparation and health-check cadence to identify regression risk, cost overruns, and performance opportunities.

Owner and primary contacts:
- Playbook owner: Priya Sharma (Customer Success Manager)
- Escalation lead: Julian Park (Support Engineering)
- SE integration lead: Anika Patel (Solutions Engineering)
- SRE escalation contact: Marco Alvarez (Eng SRE)

1) Enterprise Onboarding Checklist (high level)

Pre-contract (Sales -> CS handoff):
1. Sales to fill and upload the customer intake form (customer name, technical contact, expected QPS, privacy requirements, preferred deployment mode).
2. CS to schedule a discovery call within 3 business days.

Week 0 (Kickoff):
- Deliverables: kickoff slides, project plan, success criteria, timeline.
- Actions:
  - Introductions: CS, SE, SRE, and customer technical leads.
  - Confirm network and security requirements (VPC, IP allowlist, KMS/HSM needs).
  - Confirm model variants to be used and data residency expectations.

Integration (Week 1-2):
- Tasks:
  - Provide API key and access instructions (temporary test key + production key request workflow).
  - Share sandbox endpoint and sample prompts / evaluation prompts.
  - Perform baseline perf tests: latency p50/p95, throughput, token cost expectations.
  - Configure tracing and logs (attach trace id examples).
  - Perform authentication and authorization checks (RBAC validation).

Validation & Go-live (Week 2-4):
- Success criteria (all must be met):
  - Latency p95 within agreed SLO for chosen deployment mode.
  - Error rate < 0.5% on representative traffic for 24 hours.
  - Cost per 1k tokens within target band (as agreed from pricing guidance).
  - Monitoring and alerting configured in customer console and CS dashboards.
- Go-live steps:
  1. Confirm production API keys and rotate test keys.
  2. Schedule cutover window; communicate rollback plan.
  3. Monitor health dashboard for the first 72 hours and report daily.

Handoff to Success + Regular cadence:
- Weekly check-ins for first 30 days, then biweekly until QBR.
- Add customer to QBR rotation and monitoring alerts.

2) Integration Guide (concise technical checklist)

Essential configuration items:
- API endpoint: https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1 (use customer-specific host for private deployments)
- Auth: API Key via Authorization: Bearer <KEY> header.
- Rate limits: per-customer defaults: 100 rps; dedicated customers may have higher limits per contract.
- Model pinning: include "model": "redwood/gpt-like-1.0" in request body to pin versions.

Sample curl (text generation):
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/llm-1.0","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'

SDK snippet (Python):
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="<KEY>")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood/llm-1.0", input="Hello")

Integration validation tests (run these before go-live):
- Auth smoke test: 10 auth attempts with valid/invalid keys to confirm error codes (401 for invalid).
- Throughput test: run a 10-minute load test at 50% of expected production QPS.
- Model regression test: run canonical prompt set and compare embeddings/outputs to baseline; record quality delta.

3) Support Process and SLAs

Ticketing and triage:
- Primary support channel: Zendesk (tickets created by CS/SE or auto-created from console alerts).
- Triage within 1 business hour for severity 1/2; within 4 business hours for severity 3; within 24 business hours for general inquiries.

Severity definitions and SLAs:
| Severity | Symptom | Target initial response | Target resolution* | Escalation path |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Sev 1 (Critical) | Production outage or >20% traffic impacted | 15 minutes | 4 hours | SE -> SRE -> Eng on-call |
| Sev 2 (High) | Significant degradation (latency p95 > SLO x2, elevated error rates) | 1 hour | 24 hours | Support Eng -> SRE -> Eng owner |
| Sev 3 (Medium) | Feature-impacting but limited scope | 4 hours | 3 business days | Support -> SE |
| Sev 4 (Low) | Documentation, onboarding questions, feature requests | 1 business day | 10 business days | CS -> Product |
*Resolution targets are contractual suggestions; actual timelines depend on root cause and escalation.

Escalation matrix (quick reference):
- Level 1 (Support Engineer): initial triage, reproduce, collect logs/traces, attempt workaround.
- Level 2 (Support Engineering / SE): deeper debugging, coordinate with SRE for infra-level issues.
- Level 3 (SRE / Runtime Eng): investigate kernel/scheduling, capacity, or deployment issues.
- Level 4 (Engineering/Product): code fixes, model regressions, or platform changes.

Required ticket artifacts for escalation (always attach):
- Customer ID and environment (prod/staging)
- RequestId/traceId and timestamps (UTC)
- Example request/response payloads (with PII redacted)
- Recent cost/usage snapshot and observed QPS
- Baseline performance metrics and drift from baseline

4) Escalation Playbook (step-by-step for Sev 1/Sev 2)

Sev 1 (Production outage):
1. Immediate actions (first 15 minutes):
   - Acknowledge ticket and tag as Sev 1.
   - Notify SRE on-call and create a dedicated Incident Slack channel (#inc-<customer>-YYYYMMDD).
   - Collect initial artifacts: endpoint health, kube/pod status, GPU utilization, error logs.
2. Containment (15-60 minutes):
   - If outage is due to capacity: enable burst capacity or failover to hosted model variant.
   - If action requires customer config change, enact temporary mitigation (e.g., reduce concurrency, enable rate limiter).
3. Resolution (60-240 minutes):
   - Apply fix (traffic reroute, config change, hotfix).
   - Validate with customer using synthetic and real traffic.
   - Post-incident: document cause, steps taken, and RCA owner (within 48 hours).

Sev 2 (High severity degradation):
1. Acknowledge and triage within 1 hour.
2. Run standard perf triage checklist: check KV cache hit rate, batching configuration, model quantization mismatch, and kernel failures.
3. Escalate to SRE if infra metrics (GPU OOMs, high host load) are observed.
4. Implement mitigations (model fallback, reduce max_tokens, temporary rate-limiting).

Communication rules:
- Real-time updates every 30 minutes during Sev 1 incidents until containment.
- Status updates every 2-4 hours for Sev 2 until mitigated.
- Customer-facing postmortem to be shared within 7 business days for Sev 1; RCA summary for Sev 2 within 10 business days.

5) Known Issues and Workarounds (select examples)

- Issue: Increased p95 latency during sustained short-request workloads.
  Workaround: Apply per-connection concurrency limit and enable smaller batch windows (SE config: batch_window_ms=10). Recommend kernel tuning for short-seq optimization.

- Issue: Occasional 502s during autoscaling events in dedicated clusters.
  Workaround: Temporarily pin to a warm pool (enable warm_instances=2) and increase health check grace period to 60s. SRE to review autoscaler thresholds.

- Issue: Model output regression after model variant roll (semantic drift).
  Workaround: Roll back to previous pinned model and initiate model onboarding regression suite. Tag the rollout and block downstream traffic until evaluation passes QA.

- Issue: Private deployment KMS integration failures (timeout with HSM).
  Workaround: Verify network connectivity to customer KMS endpoints, increase TLS handshake timeout to 30s, and provide a temporary key injection process per customer-approved security exception.

Each known issue should be logged in the customer-specific "Known Issues" section of the customer record and linked to the central tracker: confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds.

6) Health Checks and QBR Materials

Standard health check cadence:
- Week 1-4 after go-live: daily health check (CS + SE).
- Month 1-3: weekly checks.
- Ongoing: monthly health checks and quarterly QBRs.

Health check checklist (examples):
- Availability: % uptime over period (target 99.9% monthly).
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for text generation and embeddings.
- Error rate: 4xx vs 5xx breakdown, target <0.5% 5xx.
- Cost: tokens per request and cost per 1k tokens vs budget.
- Model quality: drift on canonical prompt set (accuracy or ROUGE/F1 depending on use case).
- Usage patterns: QPS peaks, steady-state QPS, burst events.

QBR template (agenda):
1. Executive summary (CS): adoption highlights and risks.
2. Usage and performance metrics (SRE support): trend charts for latency, errors, and cost.
3. Feature and roadmap alignment (Product): upcoming features relevant to customer's use cases.
4. Open actions and risks (CS): outstanding escalations, security requests, and milestones.
5. Recommendations & next steps (SE): optimization opportunities (batching, quantization, model variants).

Deliverables before QBR (to be prepared 5 business days ahead):
- Health snapshot PDF with charts for last quarter.
- Regression test results for the canonical prompt set.
- Cost optimization opportunities with estimated savings.
- Action tracker with owners and due dates.

7) Templates and Quick References

Sample incident Slack message (use for Sev 1):
"@here Incident Sev1: <customer> inference outage. Channel #inc-<customer>-YYYYMMDD created. Current status: investigating. Primary contact: Julian Park. Initial hypothesis: increased queue depth during autoscaling."

QBR slide checklist (bullets):
- Title slide (date, attendees)
- Executive summary and CS health score (Red/Amber/Green)
- Technical health (latency, errors, cost)
- Integrations and open tickets
- Recommendations and action items

8) Postmortem and RCA expectations

- For Sev 1 incidents, publish a public-facing postmortem within 7 business days and a detailed internal RCA within 48 hours. The public postmortem must include: timeline, impact, root cause, remediation steps, and preventions.
- RCA owner: assigned within 2 business days and tracked in Jira (link included in ticket).
